If depth priors are used, add a self-supervised depth loss [S2]:

The claim states that if depth priors are used, a self-supervised depth loss is added. The evidence in Source [S2] explicitly describes a method where inputs are RGB images processed by a pre-trained depth network to obtain 'depth priors'. It then details the use of a 'self-supervised depth loss' ($L_{self-depth}$) which utilizes learnable parameters to undistort these prior depth maps ($D̂_{idpt}$) to match the rendered depth ($D_{infer}$ or $D_{inerf}$). The equations and text confirm that this loss is integral to the optimization process when utilizing these priors.
